title: A Choir for the Cellar
premise: Casper Zhou, a property surveyor sent to appraise Hollowmere House before its final sale, discovers the mansion is a living instrument built by its founders to harvest and store memory—every mirror lags one second behind, replaying the room with someone extra standing in it. As Casper maps the house room by room, the house maps them back, unearthing memories they buried and binding them to the founders' unfinished ritual, which requires a surveyor's signature to complete. Torn between duty to their firm, growing love for the last resident's heir, Wren Aldercott, and the house's hunger, Casper must choose whether to finish the ritual and seal the house's power forever, or destroy it and lose every recorded memory inside—including their own. In the end, Casper signs the papers with a line through the founders' clause, unbinding the house at the cost of their own reflection, which stays behind in the mirrors while they walk out with Wren into an unrecorded morning.
about_author: Xanthe Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former architectural conservator who spent a decade cataloguing derelict estates across the English coast before turning to fiction. They write horror about buildings that remember, and claim to have never slept in a house with fewer than four mirrors.

chapters.title: The Appraisal
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper Zhou arrives at Hollowmere House to conduct a pre-sale structural survey, armed with checklists and professional detachment. The house is immaculate, empty, and wrong in small ways—doors that number differently on each count. Emotional beat: quiet unease masked as professionalism; the reader senses Casper's habit of staying invisible in other people's spaces.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: POV Casper. In a bathroom mirror, Casper notices their reflection lags—a blink arriving a beat behind. They test it with a metronome app and confirm: every mirror in the house reflects the room one second late, and in that second, something else occupies the frame. Emotional beat: rational denial cracking into dread.

chapters.title: The Last Resident
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Wren Aldercott, heir to the estate, arrives to sign the sale papers, warm and grieving and determined to be rid of the house. Casper, bound by duty not to disclose anomalies, says nothing about the mirrors. Emotional beat: reluctant connection; Casper notices Wren flinches at reflections too.

chapters.title: Room by Room
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper surveys methodically, and the survey becomes a map of wrongness: a nursery that measures four inches longer at night, a hallway whose wallpaper repeats a face. The house responds to being measured—doors open ahead of Casper's hand. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing they are the specimen.

chapters.title: What the House Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren's chapter reveals childhood in Hollowmere: a grandmother who spoke to mirrors, a mother who vanished 'into the walls' of memory. Wren wants the house sold precisely because it collects people. Emotional beat: grief braided with guilt; Wren recognizes Casper's fear as familiar.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Casper. In the cellar archive, Casper finds the founders' ledger—Hollowmere was built as an engine, a ritual apparatus to store memory in glass and mortar, 'a choir of kept moments.' The final page names a required office: a surveyor's signature. Emotional beat: intellectual horror; the house was designed, not haunted.

chapters.title: Counted Doors
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper counts doors at dusk: thirty-one. At midnight: thirty-two. The extra door stands where the ledger's diagram shows the ritual chamber, and behind it, Casper hears a choir humming in their own voice. Emotional beat: the house has learned Casper's habits and is imitating intimacy.

chapters.title: Duty's Fine Print
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper's firm calls: sign the appraisal, close the sale, no anomalies on record or the contract voids and Casper's career with it. Casper lies in the report. Emotional beat: corruption of power in miniature—Casper wields institutional power and feels it curdle into complicity.

chapters.title: The Second That Isn't Yours
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren confronts Casper after finding the doctored report, and in the argument a mirror shows them both—one second late—standing closer than they are. Wren confesses the house showed them their mother's last memory. Emotional beat: love kindling inside mutual fear; the lag becomes a space where honesty is possible.

chapters.title: Choir Practice
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The mirrors begin replaying memories Casper buried: a sibling's death, a childhood promise to never be remembered. The house is tuning Casper like an instrument. Emotional beat: violated interiority; memory itself becomes the haunted ground.

chapters.title: The Aldercott Clause
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren finds the original deed: the founders bound the house to their bloodline, and every heir's signature has fed it for two centuries. Wren's mother didn't leave—she was signed in. Wren refuses to sign. Emotional beat: rage at inherited duty; the theme of love against duty sharpens.

chapters.title: Thirteen Mirrors Down
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper tries to break the house by destroying mirrors. Each shattered glass releases a stored memory into the room—centuries of kept moments howling free—until the house retaliates, sealing doors and turning the lag into two seconds, then three. Emotional beat: defiance met with escalation; the house is waking fully.

chapters.title: The Extra Door Opens
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The thirty-second door stands open. Inside is the ritual chamber: a circular room of standing mirrors, and in them, every past surveyor and heir who 'finished' or failed the founders' work. The founders' voices explain the terms: complete the ritual, and the house sleeps for another century. Emotional beat: seduction of power—the house offers Casper permanence.

chapters.title: What Casper Would Keep
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren finds Casper staring into the chamber mirrors, which show a life where Casper is remembered, celebrated, never invisible. The house is negotiating. Wren pulls them back with the plain, unmirrored truth of the present. Emotional beat: love as anchor against the corruption of offered power.

chapters.title: The Firm Arrives
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper's supervisor arrives to force the closing, dismisses the anomalies, and walks into the cellar to 'inspect'—the house takes him into the glass mid-sentence. Casper realizes the house doesn't need a signature; it needs a surveyor, any surveyor. Emotional beat: horror of institutional expendability; Casper's duty was always bait.

chapters.title: Reading the Ritual
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper deciphers the ledger's final instructions: the ritual doesn't imprison memory—it feeds the house forever, and the founders built a flaw into it, a countersign, in case their creation outgrew them. The flaw requires a surveyor to sign the papers and strike the clause. Emotional beat: grim hope; the tool of the house's completion is also its undoing.

chapters.title: The House Argues
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The house speaks through every mirror at once, using Wren's mother's voice, offering her back in exchange for Wren's signature. Wren nearly signs. Casper arrives and breaks the mirror holding the false mother. Emotional beat: the cruelest temptation; love and grief weaponized against each other.

chapters.title: Last Survey
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper performs a final, honest survey—every door counted, every mirror named, the house measured down to its foundations—because the countersign must be true. The house fights back with Casper's own buried memories, but Casper, for the first time, refuses to look away from them. Emotional beat: acceptance; Casper stops being invisible to themselves.

chapters.title: The Signing
chapters.summary: POV Casper. In the ritual chamber, Casper signs the final sale papers and draws a single line through the founders' clause. The choir screams; the mirrors show every kept memory burning free. Wren holds the pen's twin—two signatures, one act of love against two centuries of duty. Emotional beat: climax; sacrifice chosen, not imposed.

chapters.title: One Second Early
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The house exhales. Mirrors go dark, then ordinary—except one, which now runs one second early, showing the empty room before they enter it. Wren realizes what it means and runs. Emotional beat: dread transmuted into tenderness; the cost is becoming legible.

chapters.title: The Unrecorded Morning
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper walks out of Hollowmere with Wren, their reflection left behind in the glass—kept, like everything the house ever loved. Casper feels no camera, no mirror, no record holding them anymore, and finds the lightness almost indistinguishable from loss. Emotional beat: bittersweet freedom; power's price paid in permanence.

chapters.title: Coda: A Choir for the Cellar
chapters.summary: POV Wren, months later. The new owners report nothing wrong; the cellar is just a cellar. But Wren keeps one salvaged mirror in their flat, and some nights it shows a room one second late, with someone in it, humming—keeping the memory Wren couldn't carry. Emotional beat: quiet haunting; love persists as the last choir of kept things.
